mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 4% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive two-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative following two consecutive quarterly declines in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.3% in the same month signals a sharp labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3% AND PAYEMS falls > 0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises > 0.3% and PAYEMS falls > 0.3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2%) combined with a rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for three consecutive months signals a low-rate, high-inflation environment, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL > 3% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between real personal income (implied by PAYEMS trend) and S&P 500 forward returns over a 5-day horizon, such that rising payroll employment predicts near-term equity gains.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises month-over-month.
